If you only do one thing in Hanoi... attend Tuan's cooking class
Mar 2014 • Family
We requested to have a cooking lesson from the head chef here at the Rising Dragon Restaurant. The whole experience was fabulous and I could not recommend this enough. 

As someone who loves to cook, I didn't just want to be given a load of ingredients and taught the basic's of chopping and how to follow a recipe.. instead I wanted to understand the different types of ingredients and the flavours of the different types of vietnamese meals, so I could replicate these dishes back in the UK with local ingredient's available to me. Tuan was fantastic. He firstly asked us of the types of meals we were interested in, then took us to the market to get the ingredients. Here he talked through the different type of Vietnamese veg; describing what they were similar to, and how to tell if they were in ripe. 

Back in the kitchen, we made several dishes, each taught in a very professional and skill appropriate manner. Correcting and teaching us new tips on how to be more efficient with prep etc. 

The food was delicious and then served upstairs in the open air restaurant - don't expect anything fancy here.. its the local charm that sells this place. Tuan is an exceptional teacher and chef, and I believe he could tailor his teaching to any level of cook. 

I would highly recommend requesting this cooking class to anyone visiting Hanoi.

Nice meal, but save it for your last night.
May 2014 • Family
We stayed 5 nights at the Rising Dragon Palace. To be fair, we were told when we booked in that the restaurant was a top 10 restaurant in Vietnam. We wanted to sample all the local foods though, so went out for our Bun Cha, Pho, and other superb local foods. On our last night, we wanted to send our son and his fiancée off on the remainder of their trip with a good meal, so used the restaurant, and were not disappointed. The food was of a very good quality, and there was plenty of it. If you order salads for starters, you will NOT need one each, and they are high quality. The youngsters ordered steak, and it was cooked exactly how they asked it to be - and that's a rarity in most places we go. The only reason I haven't 5 starred the restaurant, the staff wanted to clear our starters away before we'd finished, which meant some nice food left on the plates. This was because they had cooked the main course, and needed to get it on the table. SLOW DOWN! 
Most enjoyable last meal in Hanoi.
